- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to avoid underestimation.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent high sentiment peaks; apply lagged smoothing: average last 3–5 forecast values before applying next period.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit recent trends; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2–4% in 2–3 subsequent periods.
- For horizon > 10 days, model tends to overestimate volatility; apply 10–15% downward adjustment for long-term forecasts if sentiment is neutral or negative.
